title: Social Identity Theory, Self-Categorisation and Intergroup Relations
summary: Social identity theory (Tajfel): social categorisation, social identification, social comparison, in-group favouritism and out-group derogation. Intergroup relations.
objectives: Explain social categorisation and social comparison.
Describe in-group favouritism and out-group derogation.
revision: Social identity theory (Tajfel): social categorisation, social comparison, in-group favouritism and intergroup relations.
traps: Social identity (Tajfel): group membership → self-esteem via in-group/out-group comparison.
In-group favouritism: preferential treatment of own group.

notes.t: The part of an individual's self-concept derived from membership in social groups, with associated value and emotional significance.
The cognitive process of classifying people into groups (in-group vs out-group) based on shared characteristics.
Comparing one's in-group favourably with relevant out-groups to enhance self-esteem.
In-group favouritism and out-group derogation follow from social categorisation and comparison, contributing to intergroup bias and conflict.

i: In-group favouritism: preferential treatment of own group
Out-group derogation: negative evaluation of other groups
Realistic conflict: competition over resources intensifies intergroup hostility
Common in-group identity: recategorisation reduces bias

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks about Tajfel's social identity theory, in-group/out-group bias and intergroup relations.

mnemonics.text: T — Tajfel (social identity theory), S — Social categorisation (in-group/out-group), C — Social comparison (self-esteem), I — In-group favouritism

flashcards.a: Self-concept from group membership with value and emotional significance.
Classifying people into in-group vs out-group.
Preferential treatment of one's own group.
